title: Version anchor exit plan and region fallthrough choreography
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers can 'anchor' a model version for long-lived routes; when that version is deprecated or unavailable in a region, current fallback behaviors are either too blunt (global fallback to lower-quality variant) or too brittle (request failures). Goal: define an exit and fallthrough choreography that preserves regional affinity and SLAs while allowing safe, observable substitutions and controlled deprecation drains.

Scope: region-aware selection of warm-standby variants, fallthrough scoring rules, a phased exit window with traffic draining, compatibility shims for API/weights differences, and operational telemetry + sigterms for rollbacks. This work touches the routing layer, variant registry, onboarding pipelines (performance profile publishing), and Console UI for pin/anchor status and deprecation timelines.

Design summary:
- Version anchor: treat the customer pin as an "anchor" with metadata that includes compatibility level, allowed substitutes, and deprecation timestamp.
- Fallthrough choreography: when anchor is unreachable in a region, route through a prioritized list (local warm-standby variant -> regional compatible variant -> cross-region same variant) using a numeric fallthrough score that considers latency SLO, model quality penalty, and cost multiplier.
- Exit window and drain: support a configurable drain window (default 72h) for deprecations where a small percent of traffic is gradually shifted to nominated substitutes while monitoring quality regressions on a holdout prompt set.
- Safety gates: require a passing compatibility check and smoke tests for any nominated substitute; automatic rollback on quality regressions beyond threshold for two consecutive intervals.
- Telemetry & observability: emit rollup metrics for anchor adherence, fallthrough ratio by region, perf delta (latency/cost), and quality deltas (eval-based). Console will show a per-route fallthrough timeline and deprecation countdown.

Implementation notes: we will extend the routing engine to accept a fallthrough policy object (policy stored as metadata keyed by anchor). A compatibility shim layer will translate minor API differences. A new background job will warm-up KV caches for warm-standby variants on anchor deprecation scheduling.

Out-of-scope: major model architecture substitutions that require contract changes (function calling changes) — these will surface as blocked substitutions and require manual migration.
acceptance_criteria: Routing engine supports per-anchor fallthrough policy with region priority ordering
Console displays anchor status, deprecation countdown, and per-region fallthrough events
Compatibility checks run automatically when a substitute is nominated and block unsafe substitutions
Automated drain job moves traffic according to configured window and can be paused/rolled back
Metrics available: anchor_adherence, fallthrough_ratio_{region}, perf_delta_ms, eval_quality_delta
End-to-end test covering regional failover from anchor -> warm-standby -> cross-region variant with simulated outages
